boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Gettysburg College rituals and recurring events, from retracing the 1863 procession to completing a ceremonial passage through Pennsylvania Hall.

cards.title: Retrace the Walk to Lincoln’s Address
cards.subtitle: First-years follow an 1863 route to Gettysburg National Cemetery
cards.notes: Begin with the class at Christ Chapel, follow the half-mile procession through town, and listen for the Gettysburg Address at the cemetery.
cards.short_summary: An incoming class reenacts the journey students and townspeople made to the National Cemetery in 1863.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College says the community gathers each fall with first-years to walk a half-mile to the National Cemetery, commemorating the 1863 journey to hear Lincoln dedicate it.
cards.access_notes: The College describes this as a fall event for first-year students and participating members of its community.

cards.title: Finish What Convocation Started
cards.subtitle: Students enter college and conclude Commencement through Penn Hall
cards.notes: Notice the architectural bookend: students pass through Pennsylvania Hall during Opening Convocation and return through it after Commencement.
cards.short_summary: A passage through Pennsylvania Hall marks both ends of the Gettysburg undergraduate experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College states that graduates process through Pennsylvania Hall after Commencement, completing a tradition begun by walking through the building at Opening Convocation.
cards.access_notes: Participation is tied to the College's Opening Convocation and Commencement ceremonies.

cards.title: Enter as a Gettysburgian
cards.subtitle: An Orientation ceremony formally welcomes the incoming class
cards.notes: Join the incoming class for its formal welcome, then watch how this opening ceremony connects symbolically with the final Commencement procession.
cards.short_summary: The College begins each new class’s shared story with a formal Orientation ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College identifies Opening Convocation as an Orientation ceremony welcoming first-year students into the College community.
cards.access_notes: This ceremony is part of Orientation and is intended primarily for incoming first-year students.

cards.title: Mark the Charter on April 7
cards.subtitle: The campus commemorates Gettysburg College’s 1832 founding
cards.notes: Look for the campus observance on or near April 7 and use it to connect today’s College with the charter of the original Pennsylvania College.
cards.short_summary: The College pauses near its charter anniversary to recognize its history and contributors.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College documents Founder's Day as an annual celebration held on or around April 7 to mark the anniversary of the College's founding and thank its contributors.
cards.access_notes: The College describes a campus-community gathering scheduled on or around April 7 each year.

cards.entity_name: GIV Day - Gettysburg Is Volunteering Day
cards.title: Turn Orientation Outward
cards.subtitle: The campus works with organizations across Adams County
cards.notes: Choose an assigned community project, follow the host organization’s guidance, and treat service as part of joining Gettysburg rather than a photo opportunity.
cards.short_summary: Orientation includes a coordinated day of work with dozens of Adams County organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College describes GIV Day as its annual Orientation community-service day, when students, faculty, and staff work at more than 45 Adams County organizations.
cards.access_notes: This is an organized Orientation service program; participants should use College-issued project assignments and instructions.

cards.title: See Lincoln Avenue Become the Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: A campus meal moves outdoors into a street-carnival setting
cards.notes: Head toward Lincoln Avenue when the festival is scheduled and explore the international cuisine and activities replacing the regular Dining Center service.
cards.short_summary: Gettysburg shifts an evening meal from Servo to a campus street carnival devoted to international food.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College calls the International Food Festival a tradition sponsored by the Campus Activities Board, during which the Dining Center closes and Lincoln Avenue becomes a street carnival serving international cuisine and treats.
cards.access_notes: The source identifies this as a campus event but does not provide a current date, admission policy, or guest-access terms.

cards.title: Dress the First Friday in Orange and Blue
cards.subtitle: School colors take over once every month
cards.notes: Wear orange and blue on the month’s first Friday, then document the moment only if everyone pictured agrees to its submission or sharing.
cards.short_summary: Gettysburgians coordinate a recurring monthly display of the College’s colors.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College says students, alumni, faculty, staff, and friends wear orange and blue on the first Friday of every month and may submit photographs and memories to the College.
cards.access_notes: The documented cadence is the first Friday of each month; photo submission is optional.

cards.title: Turn Spring Work into a Campus Showcase
cards.subtitle: Students present academic, creative, and service projects
cards.notes: Browse the spring program by discipline, select several unfamiliar presentations, and ask student presenters specific questions about their process.
cards.short_summary: One spring event gathers research, creative practice, and community work into a student showcase.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College describes Celebration as an annual spring event where students showcase work in academics, creative endeavors, and service or outreach.
cards.access_notes: The College identifies Celebration as an annual spring event; consult the current program for venues and attendance details.

cards.title: Close the Term at Stine Lake
cards.subtitle: A pre-finals weekend of concerts, food, and outdoor play
cards.notes: Check the current student schedule, gather at Stine Lake for the programmed activities, and keep the weekend compatible with the final week of classes.
cards.short_summary: The campus marks the approach of term’s end with a programmed weekend around Stine Lake.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College documents Springfest as a weekend before the final week of classes featuring concerts, free food, merriment, and play on Stine Lake.
cards.access_notes: The tradition occurs before the last week of classes; event-specific access and timing require the current College schedule.

cards.title: Let Your Professors Serve Thanksgiving
cards.subtitle: Faculty and staff bring a family-style feast to student tables
cards.notes: Arrive according to Dining Services guidance, settle in with a table group, and watch faculty and staff swap classroom roles for serving aprons.
cards.short_summary: Servo becomes a shared Thanksgiving table where College employees serve students the meal.
cards.evidence_claim: Gettysburg College documents Servo Thanksgiving as a full Thanksgiving dinner shared by students with friends and served by professors; a College history says the tradition has endured for decades.
cards.source_title: Servo Thanksgiving through the decades - Gettysburg College
cards.access_notes: This student dining tradition is held in the fall; current attendance and meal-plan requirements should be checked with Dining Services.
